- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast decline to 1–3% below peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.20) and price is trending up, model often underestimates continuation — add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- Model frequently overestimates mean reversion after strong moves — if price deviates > 3% from 18-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.20–0.40), model tends to smooth out extremes — avoid overfitting to recent highs/lows; use 3-day weighted average for smoothing.
- Forecast horizon > 14 days shows persistent lag — adjust for 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment turns negative after a positive trend, model often fails to recognize reversal — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days, then allow gradual reversion.
